solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Two insects circling horse that's monstrous

definitions.note: the answer is a noun: something that is monstrous

indicators.note: the two insects go round the horse, so their letters close around it

parts.note: a bee and a moth, two flying insects side by side
H is slang shorthand for heroin, called horse

explanation.surface: Someone is appalled at a horse being pestered by a pair of buzzing insects.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circling' puts H inside BEE, before MOTH.
explanation.definitionFit: A behemoth is a huge, monstrous creature, named after the biblical beast.

clue.text: Mouthpiece separate: might player want more than this?

definitions.text: might player want more than this?
definitions.note: the answer is a noun phrase: a role the player would like to be bigger

parts.note: a bit is the mouthpiece of a horse's bridle
to part is to separate

explanation.surface: An actor's mouthpiece speaks up: surely the player deserves more than a small role?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mouthpiece' hints at a spokesperson, but it is the horse's bit.
explanation.definitionFit: A bit part is a minor acting role with few lines, so an actor would want a larger one.

clue.text: Track down missing note in cabin

indicators.note: the word for track down goes without the note letter, which is removed

parts.note: to hunt is to track down

explanation.surface: Someone tracks down a missing note left in a cabin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missing' removes N from HUNT.
explanation.definitionFit: A hut is a small simple shelter, much like a cabin.

clue.text: Crucible girl can put on good snooker shot

parts.note: Mel is a girl's name
a tin is a can
a pot is a shot sinking a ball in snooker

explanation.surface: A girl at the Crucible, home of world snooker, pulls off a good shot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crucible' evokes Sheffield's Crucible Theatre, where the World Snooker Championship is played, but it is the vessel. MEL + TIN + G + POT.
explanation.definitionFit: A melting pot, like a crucible, is a vessel in which substances are melted and fused.

clue.text: Money short then endlessly given in tax

indicators.note: short means the word for money is cut, losing its last letter

parts.note: tin is old slang for money

indicators.note: endlessly means the word then loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Money ran short, then was paid out in tax without end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'short' cuts TIN to TI; 'endlessly' cuts THEN to THE.
explanation.definitionFit: A tithe was a tenth of produce paid as a tax to support the church.

clue.text: Package right put in place for sorting

indicators.note: letters needing sorting are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A parcel goes to its proper place in the depot to be sorted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for sorting' rearranges R plus PLACE.
explanation.definitionFit: A parcel is a wrapped package sent by post, so the two are synonyms.

clue.text: Analyst's initial manner is remote

indicators.note: initial means the first letter of the word it goes with

parts.note: a way is a manner of doing something

explanation.surface: A psychoanalyst's opening manner comes across as distant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initial' takes A from Analyst's.
explanation.definitionFit: Away means at a distance, far off, which is to say remote.

clue.text: Elegantly smart acquaintance paid a pittance

parts.note: chic means stylishly elegant
ken is knowledge or acquaintance, as in beyond my ken
feed is a playful form of fee'd, given a fee

explanation.surface: A smartly dressed friend got paid next to nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: FEED here is read as fee'd, given a fee, so paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Chicken feed is an idiom for a trivially small sum of money.

clue.text: Small child stuck in helmet that's narrow

indicators.note: the child is lodged inside the word for helmet

parts.note: lid is slang for a helmet or hat
a mite is a small child

explanation.surface: A toddler has got stuck inside a helmet that is too narrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Limited means restricted in scope, so narrow, as in a narrow or limited view.

clue.text: Staunch supporter certain at heart to regret waste

indicators.note: at heart means the centre letter of the word certain

parts.note: to rue is to regret
to blue money is to squander it

explanation.surface: A loyal fan is certain, deep down, to regret wasting their money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' takes T, the middle letter of certain. To blue is British slang for squandering money.
explanation.definitionFit: A true blue is a dyed-in-the-wool loyalist, especially a staunch Conservative.

clue.text: Limitation as art reworked in autocratic approach

indicators.note: something reworked is made again in a fresh form, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A critic complains that limiting art is the method of a dictatorial regime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reworked' rearranges LIMITATION AS ART.
explanation.definitionFit: Totalitarianism is a system of government by one all-controlling authority, an autocratic way of ruling.

clue.text: Mathematician once corresponded in a matter of law

indicators.note: the word for corresponded is set in the middle of the other pieces

parts.note: res is the Latin legal term for a thing or matter
chimed means agreed or matched up

explanation.surface: A long-dead mathematician agreed with someone on a point of law.
explanation.walkthrough: RES, Latin for 'thing', is a standard legal term (as in res judicata).
explanation.definitionFit: Archimedes was an ancient Greek mathematician, so he is a mathematician of long ago.

clue.text: Diabolical cur: damnable one made to support the wicked?

definitions.text: one made to support the wicked?
definitions.note: the answer is a noun: a thing made to hold up wicks

indicators.note: something diabolical is badly messed up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A devilish dog is cursed as a creature built to back wrongdoers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diabolical' rearranges CUR DAMNABLE. 'The wicked' reads as evildoers, but punningly means things with wicks, i.e. candles.
explanation.definitionFit: A candelabrum is a branched holder for several candles, each with a wick.

clue.text: Hold meeting to involve king in satirical piece

indicators.note: the meeting word takes in the king, holding it inside

parts.note: a committee or court sits when it is in session
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A meeting called to bring in the king becomes the subject of satire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to involve' puts K inside SIT.
explanation.definitionFit: A skit is a short comic sketch that parodies or satirises something.

clue.text: Cardcastle collapsed in game

indicators.note: a collapsed structure falls apart, so its letters are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: A house of cards falls down in the middle of a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collapsed' rearranges CARDCASTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cat's cradle is a children's string game played by looping string between the fingers.

clue.text: Drunk goes around talking about this evening

indicators.note: the word for drunk wraps round the word for talking about

parts.note: tight is informal for drunk
on, as in a lecture on a subject, means about

explanation.surface: A drunk wanders around rambling about what is happening this evening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' looks like the anagram signal; it is the synonym TIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonight means during the present or coming night, i.e. this evening.

clue.text: Being dry, wild duck swallows energy drink

indicators.note: the duck takes the other pieces inside it, as if gulping them down

parts.note: the teal is a small wild duck
E is the physics symbol for energy
a tot is a small drink of spirits

explanation.surface: A wild duck gulps an energy drink, despite being a non-drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A teetotal person abstains from alcohol, so is dry in that sense.

clue.text: Composer shown way outside having great knowledge

indicators.note: the word for shown the way sits around the composer

parts.note: led means guided, shown the way
Thomas Arne was the English composer of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A composer is shown the way out by a well-informed guide.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer is read as two syllables, LEARN-ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned describes a scholarly person with deep knowledge.

clue.text: Expert needing to make firm solvent

parts.note: an ace is an expert
to tone muscles is to make them firm

explanation.surface: A specialist needs to firm up a company that has become solvent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solvent' suggests a financially sound firm; here it is the chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Acetone is a chemical solvent, used for instance in nail-polish remover.

clue.text: Hindenberg for example spreads with it

parts.note: airs means broadcasts or spreads, as in airs one's views
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: The Hindenburg disaster is an example that spreads with it everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spreads' reads as a verb of motion; it means airs, as in voicing or broadcasting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hindenburg was a famous German zeppelin, a passenger airship, destroyed by fire in 1937.

clue.text: Devil leaving Black Death region in London

indicators.note: black departs from the word for devil, so its letter is taken away

parts.note: the Beast is a name for the Devil in Revelation
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black
end means death

explanation.surface: The plague, a devil of a thing, leaves a district of London.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaving' removes B from BEAST, giving EAST. The EAST END is the historically working-class district of east London.
explanation.definitionFit: The East End is a well-known district of London, east of the City.

clue.text: Bass note heard in the remotest ocean?

parts.note: a bass voice is deep

indicators.note: heard signals that the note's name is sounded out, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: C is a musical note, whose name sounds like sea

explanation.surface: A low note sounds across the farthest reaches of the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heard' gives SEA for the note C.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-sea describes the far depths of the ocean, the parts most remote from the surface.

clue.text: Bay tree lacking in width

indicators.note: the tree is without the width letter, so it is removed

parts.note: the rowan is the mountain ash

explanation.surface: A bay tree is described as lacking in width, a slim specimen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bay tree' reads as one plant; 'Bay' is a horse colour and 'tree' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay and roan are both horse coats, so a roan stands for a bay as another horse of that kind.

clue.text: Pay for game that provides a walkover?

definitions.note: the answer is a noun: a thing that provides a way to walk over

parts.note: to foot the bill is to pay for it
bridge is a card game

explanation.surface: Someone pays to enter a game that turns out to be an easy win.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Walkover' means an easy win, but the question mark points to a literal walk over something.
explanation.definitionFit: A footbridge carries pedestrians over a road or river, providing a way to walk across.

clue.text: Fish seen regularly in Trent area

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A fish is spotted often in the River Trent's waters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes T, E, T, R, A from Trent area. The Trent is a major English river.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetra is a small tropical freshwater fish, popular in aquariums.

clue.text: Ground outside hard, but provided with boots

indicators.note: the word for ground goes around the letter for hard

parts.note: sod is turf, the ground
H is the pencil-grade abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: The ground outdoors is hard, but the walkers have boots on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' puts H inside SOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Shod means wearing shoes or boots, as a horse is fitted with shoes.

clue.text: Maybe Iago's characteristic Richardson exemplifies?

definitions.meaning: Iago, the villain of Othello, shows pitiless cruelty, a lack of feeling
the name has the word for unfeeling at its heart: RIC-HARD-SON

explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is a playful one: HARD sits in the middle of RICHARDSON, so the name is literally 'hard-hearted', with no slight on any actual Richardson.
explanation.definitionFit: Hard-heartedness is callous cruelty, the quality of Shakespeare's scheming villain Iago.

clue.text: Measure height missed in the lower regions

indicators.note: the height letter is missed out of the underworld word, so it is removed

parts.note: hell is the underworld, the nether regions

explanation.surface: A measurement of height is missing down in the depths.
explanation.walkthrough: 'missed' removes H from HELL.
explanation.definitionFit: An ell is an old unit of length for cloth, about 45 inches.

clue.text: Mystery writer covering bananas in fragrant ointment

indicators.note: the writer's name wraps over the word for bananas

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe wrote early detective and mystery stories
bananas is slang for mad

explanation.surface: A crime novelist is smeared with mashed bananas in a sweet-smelling cream.
explanation.definitionFit: Pomade is a scented oil or cream for dressing the hair.

clue.text: One put to bed happened to have a bad back

parts.note: came, as in came about, means happened

indicators.note: back means the pair of pieces is read in reverse order

parts.note: ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: Someone was sent to bed because they turned out to have a bad back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns A + ILL into LLIA. 'Put to bed' suggests a tired person; it is a shrub planted in a flower bed.
explanation.definitionFit: A camellia is a flowering shrub, the sort of plant a gardener puts in a bed.
